slot.brief: Given ΔH° and ΔS° for a reaction, compute ΔG° and the equilibrium temperature at which it becomes spontaneous — numeric via ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.

stem: For a reaction, $\Delta H^\circ = 40\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = 200\ \text{J K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$. The value of $\Delta G^\circ$ at $27^\circ\text{C}$ and the temperature condition for the reaction to be spontaneous are, respectively:
working:
$T = 27^\circ\text{C} = 300\ \text{K}$.  
$\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ = 40\times10^3\ \text{J} - (300\ \text{K})(200\ \text{J K}^{-1}) = 40\,000 - 60\,000 = -20\,000\ \text{J} = -20\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.  
At equilibrium $\Delta G^\circ = 0$: $T = \Delta H^\circ/\Delta S^\circ = 40\,000/200 = 200\ \text{K}$.  
Since $\Delta H^\circ > 0$ and $\Delta S^\circ > 0$, the reaction is spontaneous ($\Delta G^\circ < 0$) when $T > 200\ \text{K}$. Hence option (A).
solution: At $27^\circ\text{C}=300\,\text{K}$, $\Delta G^\circ=\Delta H^\circ-T\Delta S^\circ=40-(300)(0.200)=-20\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The threshold temperature is $T=\Delta H^\circ/\Delta S^\circ=40{,}000/200=200\,\text{K}$; since $\Delta H^\circ,\Delta S^\circ>0$, the reaction is spontaneous for $T>200\,\text{K}$.
